case_title: Randhir @ Randhir Pal & Ors. v. State of Haryana
accused_caste: Brahaman (described for Randhir (A2) and Shiv Narain (A8); the judgment also describes Lakhmi Ram (A7) as Brahaman by caste)
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity: the alleged motive was an earlier murder (of Prem s/o Baru, 30.8.2001) in which the victim was allegedly involved; appellants are relatives of that deceased
statutory_provisions: IPC s.148, s.302, s.342, s.452 read with s.149; Arms Act (charged against Satpal A1 only, not the appellants)
weapon: Country-made pistol, knives and gandasas (axes), alleged as carried by the six assailants inside the shop
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony of two brothers of the deceased; complaint/FIR; site plan Ex.PC and rough sketch map
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.148, 302, 342, 452 read with s.149 (sentence not stated in judgment)
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 715 DB/2004) dismissed; conviction upheld
neutral_facts: On the morning of the occurrence, the victim was at a shop with his two brothers. According to a complaint lodged the same day, six men entered the shop carrying a country-made pistol, knives and axes. One of them fired a shot that struck the victim in the chest, and others struck the victim with axes and a knife on the face, shoulder and ear. The assailants then left the shop. The complaint further alleged that five other men stood outside the shop and in the street, preventing people from entering the shop and passersby from moving along the street. The complaint was converted into a First Information Report. Two of the victim's brothers testified as eyewitnesses. One brother described the five men as armed with lathis and pitchforks and said they stopped three named persons from approaching the shop. Those three persons were not named in the original complaint and were not recorded during the investigation. The other brother said he had gone to his field to call for help and returned with those same persons. The victim died from his injuries. A site plan marked the positions of the five men outside the shop. The prosecution case placed the motive in an earlier killing involving a relative of the victim.
physical_harm: Victim died; fatal gunshot to the chest and axe and knife injuries to face, shoulder and ear (alleged)
number_of_offences: 4 charged (ss.148, 302, 342, 452, each read with s.149); 0 finally upheld for these appellants
motive: alleged: revenge for the earlier murder of Prem s/o Baru (30.8.2001), in which the victim was allegedly involved
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness accounts (PW7, PW8) that the five appellants were not involved in the assault inside the shop and caused no injuries; FIR did not say the appellants were armed; State's concession that none of the five participated inside the shop
witness_credibility: PW7's added account of persons being stopped was an afterthought, not in the FIR, and was demolished by PW8's statement; found doubtful and not fully established
bail_history: Appellants were on bail at the Supreme Court stage; bail bonds discharged on acquittal
trial_duration: offence: 26.11.2002; trial judgment: 23.7.2004; High Court: 18.9.2009; Supreme Court: 06.10.2016
legal_representation: Accused: V. Giri, Sr. Adv., with Mrs. Kawaljit Kochar, Ms. Krishna Parkhari, Ms. Kusum Chaudhary (Advs.). State: Anish Kumar Gupta, AAG, with Chandra Shekhar Suman, R. K. Rajwanshi, Ms. Deepshikha Bharati, Dr. Monika Gusain (Advs.)
investigation_status: FIR registered on same-day complaint; site plan Ex.PC prepared; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Persons allegedly stopped from entering or passing were never examined during investigation or trial; new names added later at trial, not in FIR
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted; High Court: appeal dismissed 18.9.2009; Supreme Court: appellants acquitted (benefit of doubt); co-accused's SLP dismissed 22.2.2010
prosecution_argument: Appellants' positions were shown in the site plan Ex.PC at points J and K; the State disputed that their position was absent from the rough sketch map
defence_argument: Appellants were not alleged to have entered the shop, assaulted the deceased, been armed or caused injuries; the named persons were an afterthought; motive was enmity and family members were roped in
legal_principle_applied: Benefit of doubt: where involvement cannot be established with certainty, accused are acquitted
